newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, PLO delegates may meet again on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Israel, PLO delegates may meet again on Thursday.

text.p: Israeli and Palestinian negotiators, who tried on Sunday to put peace talks back on track, could meet again on Thursday, a senior Palestinian official said on Monday.

Tayeb Abdel-Rahim, secretary-general of Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's office, expressed surprise at comments by Egyptian and Israeli officials that progress had been made in Sunday's talks in Cairo.
"But in any case, it seems that there will be another meeting next Thursday and it will be a three-way meeting," he told Israeli Arabic radio.
Michael Stoltz, a spokesman for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, said no meeting had been scheduled yet. "But I wouldn't rule one out," Stoltz told Reuters.
Peace talks have been frozen since Israel began a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March. Palestinians have demanded Israel halt construction before peace talks can resume.
Egypt has been mediating between Israel and the Palestinians to revive the negotiations.
